source.quote: ## 2. Exact reduction to a flux-sensitive rotor, not a harmonic truncation
source.range_scope: Exact compact fiber, phase stiffness, necessary barrier and explicit matching attainer.

source_excerpts.text:
## 2. Exact reduction to a flux-sensitive rotor, not a harmonic truncation

Use psi=phi-gY and Fourier transform the remaining helical translation.
Its conserved momentum is P=p_Y+gL_phi. The exact fiber Hamiltonian is

    H(P)=P^2/(2B)+(L_phi-hbar q(P))^2/(2I_perp)+V(psi),
    I_perp=B_0 I/B,
    q(P)=g I P/(hbar B).                              (3)

In particular the NORMAL recoil scale is

    E_R=hbar^2/(2I_perp)=hbar^2 B/(2B_0 I).            (4)

No angle has been unwrapped and no high rotor state was discarded. Let
epsilon(q) be the lowest eigenvalue of the periodic operator
E_R(-i partial_psi-q)^2+V(psi). Its zero-flux ground state psi_0 is real,
strictly positive and nondegenerate. The lowest helical dispersion is

    E_0(P)=P^2/(2B)+epsilon(q(P)).                     (5)

Define the measurable low-band inertia by E_0''(0)=1/B_eff. This is an
exact band response. Equating it to an entire open-contact finite-frequency
susceptibility would require additional preparation/projection estimates.

## 3. An exact ground-density formula for the actually reflected inertia

Normalize int_0^(2pi) psi_0^2=1 and define the one-dimensional phase stiffness

    f=(2pi)^2/[int psi_0^2 int psi_0^-2],  0<f<=1.      (6)

Then epsilon''(0)=2E_R f. A short derivation is worth retaining. At small
flux, the first derivative of the ground vector is purely imaginary, so
write its phase correction as psi_0 exp(iq chi). The exact second-order
ground-energy minimization is

    epsilon''(0)/2=E_R inf_(periodic real chi)
                         int psi_0^2(chi'-1)^2.

Stationarity gives psi_0^2(chi'-1)=constant. Periodicity fixes the constant
to -2pi/int psi_0^-2 and yields (6). Real amplitude changes start at order
q^2 and their contribution cancels by ground-state stationarity. This is
the standard one-dimensional phase-twist/Leggett functional, derived here
for the actual single-rotor fiber. Cauchy-Schwarz gives f<=1; positivity on
the compact circle gives f>0 for every finite smooth lock.

Using (3)-(6) gives the exact interpolation

    1/B_eff=f/B_0+(1-f)/B,
    B_eff/B=1/[1+(R-1)f], R=B/B_0.                    (7)

For no lock f=1 and B_eff=B_0, even if the formal geometric gain is huge.
The ideal constrained value B requires the periodic flux dispersion to
be suppressed to order1/R. Merely small local angle fluctuations or a
finite normal-mode gap is not that condition

source_excerpts.text:
## 1. The normal gap has an elementary uniform lower bound

At zero flux, the ground density is
rho_b(psi)=exp(2b cos psi)/(2pi I_0(2b)), b>=0. It decreases monotonically
on[0,pi] and increases on[-pi,0]. For a periodic H^1 function u and
0<=x<=pi,

    |u(x)-u(0)|^2<=x int_0^x |u'(t)|^2 dt.

Since rho_b(x)<=rho_b(t) for0<=t<=x, multiply by rho_b(x), integrate and
exchange the order to obtain

    int_0^pi rho_b|u-u(0)|^2
          <=(pi^2/2)int_0^pi rho_b|u'|^2.

The same holds on the other half circle. Weighted variance is no larger
than the squared distance from the chosen constant u(0). Thus

    Var_(rho_b)(u)<=(pi^2/2)int rho_b|u'|^2.

The ground-state transform of h_b(0)-E_R b is exactly
E_R int rho_b|u'|^2. By minmax the FULL first normal excitation gap obeys

    gap_b(0)>=2E_R/pi^2,  ALL b>=0.                    (1)

This includes every rotor harmonic, not a local-curvature estimate.

## 2. A useful entire momentum window remains gapped

For0<a<1, the form inequality

    (N-q)^2>=(1-a)N^2-q^2(1/a-1)

and V_b>=0 imply
e_1(q)>=(1-a)e_1(0)-E_R q^2(1/a-1).
The real zero-flux ground trial gives e_0(q)<=E_R(b+q^2). Therefore

    gap_b(q)/E_R>=2(1-a)/pi^2-a b-q^2/a.

Take a=1/[8pi^2(b+1)]. If

    |q|<=1/[8pi^2 sqrt(b+1)],

then a b<=1/(8pi^2), q^2/a<=1/(8pi^2), and a<3/8. Hence

    gap_b(q)>=E_R/pi^2.                               (2)

Fix a target b_*, and choose a finite momentum window |P|<=P_*
whose q(P) satisfies this condition with b=b_*. It then satisfies(2)
along the ENTIRE ramp0<=b<=b_*.
For the compact fixed-I, large-g family and any fixed P_*, q(P_*) is
O(1/g), while the allowed window shrinks only as1/sqrt(log B). Thus a
fixed finite input wavepacket fits for every sufficiently large gain.
The alternative large-I/fixed-g route may require a different momentum
stock under this deliberately conservative window bound.

## 3. Explicit input and finite ramp

An allowed initial stock is the rotor angular-momentum state N=0 and an
independent relative wavepacket with momentum amplitude

    f(P)=P_*^-1/2 cos(pi P/(2P_*)), |P|<=P_*,
    f(P)=0 otherwise.

It has norm1, finite initial variance
Var(Y)=hbar^2 pi^2/(4P_*^2), and finite momentum second moment. Smooth
stock approximations with a separately bounded state error also work.

## 1. The WHOLE lowest dispersion has an exact quadratic bracket

Let chi be the periodic real phase corrector used in the stiffness proof:

    chi'=1-[2pi/(int psi_b^-2)]psi_b^-2.

For ANY real q, psi_b exp(iq chi) is a periodic trial state. Its energy
is EXACTLY epsilon_b(0)+E_R f_b q^2, not a Taylor approximation. The
diamagnetic inequality gives the matching lower bound epsilon_b(q)>=
epsilon_b(0). Therefore the complete lowest helical dispersion satisfies

    P^2/(2B)<=E_0(P)-E_R b
                         <=[1+(R-1)f_b]P^2/(2B).      (1)

This holds across a finite momentum window without differentiating a tiny
numerical band width. Thus on that band a free hold of duration t has
unitary error, relative to the inertial evolution P^2/(2B), at most

    e_hold<=t P_*^2(R-1)f_b/(2hbar B)                  (2)

on |P|<=P_*. This compares the full ground-band phase, not merely its
second derivative at zero. With b=(1/4+epsilon)log R and t proportional
to B, (2) tends to zero.

## 2. The finite normal ramp can also preserve the known packet phase

The earlier normal preparation gave leakage amplitude a_*=hbar C_ad/T
uniformly at EVERY time during the ramp and every allowed momentum. Let
the instantaneous normalized ground vector be in parallel-transport gauge.
Writing the exact phase-removed vector as A(s)|0_s>+eta_s gives

    A'(s)=<partial_s 0_s|eta_s>,
    ||eta_s||<=a_*, ||partial_s 0_s||<=D_1/G.

Consequently the full vector differs from its adiabatic ground-band
transport, including phase, by at most a_*(1+D_1/G). Choose

    T>=hbar C_ad(1+D_1/G)/e_coh.                       (3)

All normal H_b(q) matrices are real in the Fourier basis (their cosine
couplings are real). Their rank-one eigenvectors can be chosen real and
continuous in the permitted (b,q) rectangle, so their b-Berry connection
is zero. There is no hidden phase oracle in that assertion.

For the ramp b(s)=s b, subtract its momentum-independent energy phase.
Equation(1), with f<=1, bounds the remaining phase by
